arguments.summary: Decision: develop differentiated, evidence-linked 21/63-session research theses for ANET, QQQ, MU, META and NVDA versus declared benchmarks, without return forecasts, forced rankings, or calibrated confidence. Four grouped assignments cover company/ETF look-through, macro, technical, and geopolitical channels. Commodities is omitted at planning because no direct commodity-linked decision channel is established across this primarily technology/communications watchlist; later evidence may reopen it.

claims.text: The eventual decision framework will compare company-specific catalysts and risks, dated QQQ holdings concentration, common macro/policy transmission, and 21/63-session market/technical context; it will preserve insufficient-evidence outcomes where critical inputs remain missing.

gaps.description: Planning-stage evidence has not yet been evaluated; pending specialist work is required before instrument-level assessments, valuation discussion, or differentiated theses.

assumptions: The stated 21- and 63-session horizons govern the research framing.
SPY and the specified sector ETFs are comparison context rather than forecasts or allocation recommendations.
Commodities is not presently a material standalone research stream; this omission should be revisited if company, macro, or geopolitical evidence establishes a direct transmission channel.
arguments.counter_thesis: A common technology-risk regime, policy shock, or incomplete underlying data could dominate purported company differentiation; the completed research must test rather than assume idiosyncratic drivers.

review_conditions.description: Review the integrated evidence after company, macro, technical, and geopolitical assignments complete; determine whether any instrument retains a critical evidence gap.
